newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks slip as government rules out rescue.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks slip as government rules out rescue.

text.p: Tokyo stocks faltered after another rocky ride Tuesday, buffeted by unfounded rumours of government rescue measures and a fall in the yen.
The 225-share Nikkei average, after swaying up and down, finished with a loss of 122.18 points, or 0.70 percent, at 17,358.16 -- after shedding more than 3 percent Monday.
"We're treading on thin ice and the market is bracing itself for a fall below 17,000," a strategist at one brokerage said.

The Nikkei slumped at the start of trade, undermined by fears that foreign investors would dump their Japanese shares rather than see the home-currency value of those holdings fall further as the yen weakens.

Stocks then jumped briefly into positive territory on bargain-hunting and on talk that the Finance Ministry was poised to unveil special steps to prop up share prices -- only to slide again after an official denial.
